subject: general
question: Saltoro Kangri Peak are located on which of the following borders?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Pak border**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saltoro Kangri is the highest peak in the Saltoro Mountains, a subrange of the Karakoram range.
 
• The peak is located near the actual ground position line (AGPL) which is a demarcation between Indian and Pakistani-controlled territories in the Siachen Glacier region.
 
• Saltoro Kangri is part of the larger region disputed between India and Pakistan, specifically in the Siachen Glacier area of the Karakoram range.
 
• The strategic importance of the region has led to military presence from both nations in the area, making it one of the highest battlegrounds in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saltoro Kangri:**

 
 
• Saltoro Kangri is divided into two main peaks: Saltoro Kangri I and Saltoro Kangri II.
 
• Saltoro Kangri I stands at an elevation of 7,742 meters (25,400 feet), making it the 31st highest independent peak in the world.
 
• The first successful ascent of Saltoro Kangri was made in 1962 by a Japanese-Pakistani expedition.
 
• The mountain is part of the Saltoro Ridge, which runs parallel to the Siachen Glacier, the longest glacier in the Karakoram range.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Pak Border:**
 
 
• The Indo-Pak border is one of the most heavily militarized international boundaries in the world.
 
• The border stretches for approximately 3,323 kilometers (2,065 miles) and runs through various terrains including deserts, mountains, and rivers.
 
• The Line of Control (LoC) separates the Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir from Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
 
• Several conflicts have occurred along the border, with the region of Kashmir being a major point of contention between the two countries.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Siachen Glacier:**
 
 
• The Siachen Glacier is located in the eastern Karakoram range in the Himalayas, and it is the second-longest glacier in the world's non-polar areas.
 
• Control over the glacier gives strategic advantage due to its high altitude, providing monitoring capabilities over both Indian and Pakistani territories.
 
• The region has been a site of intermittent conflict since 1984 when India launched Operation Meghdoot to gain control over the glacier.
 
• Due to the extreme conditions and high altitude, the Siachen Glacier is considered one of the most challenging military deployments in the world.
